claims.text: The nanoparticles are CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticles synthesized by chemical reduction.
The as-synthesized nanoparticles initially have well-defined surface atomic order.
Increasing local atomic disorder at the nanoparticle surface lowers the local melting barrier.
Increasing anharmonic vibrational amplitude at the nanoparticle surface lowers the local melting barrier.
A lower local melting barrier causes surface premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
Disordered surface sites exhibit enhanced and more anharmonic atomic vibrations.
Surface atomic disorder can be quantified using pair-correlation-function metrics.
Lower pair-correlation peak intensity indicates higher surface disorder.
CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles with higher surface disorder will premelt at lower temperatures than otherwise comparable nanoparticles with well-ordered surfaces.
CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles with higher vibrational amplitude will premelt at lower temperatures than nanoparticles with lower vibrational amplitude.
TEM contrast changes can serve as indications of surface premelting.
Observable surface-atom rearrangements can serve as indications of surface premelting.
Nanoparticles with well-ordered surfaces undergo premelting only near the nominal melting temperature predicted by established thermodynamic models.
The proposed disorder-controlled behavior should hold for CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles over the tested size range under high-vacuum incremental heating.
The accuracy of MD interatomic potentials may limit prediction of anharmonic vibrational behavior.
TEM sensitivity may be insufficient to distinguish subtle vibrational disorder.
